answer: Each identity opens one challenge chain, locking 60 credits and posting its head in the grove registry; each link answers a fresh challenge chained to the prior hash. A broken, forked, or reused chain loses its bond; sparrow auditors sample links; a fork burns the bond, paying the auditor 20 credits. A rented chain fails: the next challenge is unpredictable and its key cannot transfer without breaking the link. The shale archive keeps hashes and catches reuse; the k-th fake needs a 60-credit bond and chain, so 1,000 fakes lock 60,000 credits, while an honest agent keeps one 60-credit chain.
